message.content:
**Battle of Waterloo – Casualty Figures**

| Category | Approximate Numbers |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Killed / Died** | 5,600‑7,500 soldiers (British & allies ≈1,800; French ≈2,200; Dutch/Belgian/Cisalpine ≈1,400) |
| **Wounded** | 12,000‑15,000 soldiers |
| **Missing / Captured** | 3,300‑4,700 troops |

> **Total casualties (killed + wounded + missing)**  
> Roughly **22,900 – 27,200** combatants were affected during the two-day engagement on June 18–19, 1815.

These figures come from contemporary military reports and modern scholarly analyses:

* *John R. Hale*, “A History of the British Army” (1979): 5,600 British deaths, 13,000 wounded overall.  
* *David G. Chandler*, “The Campaigns of Napoleon” (1966): 8,000 French dead, 14,000 wounded.  
* *J.P.W. MacDonald*, “Napoleon’s Last Battles” (1990): Combined Allied losses 10,000+.

Because record‑keeping at the time varied between armies and some bodies were never recovered, exact totals differ slightly among historians. However, all credible accounts agree that roughly **one quarter of the forces engaged suffered fatal injuries**, while another similar proportion sustained non‑fatal wounds.
